title: call, apply, bind
concept: call, apply, and bind let you explicitly specify what this should be

steps.title: Define the greet Function
steps.explanation:
Define a greet function that uses this.name.
This function takes two arguments.

steps.title: Create Objects
steps.explanation:
Create two objects: user and admin.
We'll use these objects as this.

steps.title: call() — Pass this and Arguments Individually
steps.explanation: The call() method **immediately executes** the function, forcing the first argument to be used as **this**.
steps.keyInsight: call(this, args) = "Execute right now using this object as this!"

steps.title: apply() — Pass this and Arguments as an Array
steps.explanation: apply() takes this as the first argument and an array of arguments as the second.
steps.keyInsight: apply(thisArg, [arg1, arg2, ...]) — pass arguments as an array
steps.analogy: The difference between call and apply: call = Comma, apply = Array

steps.title: bind() — Return a New Function
steps.explanation:
bind() returns a new function with this fixed to the specified object.
It does not execute immediately!
steps.keyInsight: bind(thisArg, arg1, ...) — returns a new function (does NOT execute immediately)

steps.title: Call the Bound Function
steps.explanation:
Call boundGreet.
this is already fixed to user, and greeting is already fixed to 'Hey'.

quiz.explanation:
bind() has locked this to obj.
Even when called as a method on another object, this does not change.
Therefore obj.value * 2 = 20.

misconceptions.correct:
bind() returns a new function.
The original function is unchanged.
misconceptions.why: bind() creates and returns a new function without modifying the original.

misconceptions.wrong: call() and apply() produce different results
misconceptions.correct:
call() and apply() produce the same result.
Only the way arguments are passed differs.
misconceptions.why:
call passes arguments individually, apply passes them as an array.
The result is identical.

keyTakeaway: call(this, a, b), apply(this, [a, b]), bind(this) → returns a new function
